reviews.one_line_contribution: The claim is that the presence of an answer-bearing retrieved experience item in the demonstration slot causally suppresses per-episode compliance with an explicit, contemporaneous verification instruction — even on episodes where the agent does not copy the memory — and that instructions optimized with a bank in context therefore become bank-specific rather than generally better.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067 (experience-following), which the proposal concedes and tries to defeat with the non-echo subset test. The threat is larger than conceded. Experience-following is a graded similarity effect between retrieved output and emitted output, not a binary echo/non-echo switch. An agent can be pulled toward a stored answer, terminate its search early, and still emit a non-identical final answer — partial imitation, a stored answer that is wrong for this instance, or a paraphrase that the MEMORY-ECHO judge scores as non-matching. A surviving compliance deficit on the non-echo subset is therefore fully consistent with a graded output-imitation account, so Prediction 8 does not discriminate the two theories in the direction claimed; only a null there is informative, and the proposal has arranged its decisive test so that the outcome it predicts is the uninformative one. Worse, 'non-echo' is defined by an outcome that memory itself causes: the subset is selected post-treatment in the M1 arm and compared against unselected M0 episodes on the same instances. That is collider conditioning of exactly the kind the proposal itself disclaims in Risk 4 and Analysis 1, committed in the headline discriminating analysis. Separately, arXiv:2608.16032 ('Proof-of-Execution Memory') collides at symptom level and is handled well via the record-correctness audit, but I cannot verify that this ID exists (see preprint_collision).
reviews.strongest_objection: The centerpiece compliance measure is not separable from the mediator it is supposed to be independent of, so the 'veto' may be a relabeling of early termination rather than an instruction-slot phenomenon. I* requires the agent to cite spans retrieved in THIS episode that support the answer, and CITATION VALIDITY requires those spans to actually support it. Prediction 2 simultaneously asserts that evidence sufficiency drops >=12 points under M1. But an agent that truncated its search and never retrieved a supporting span CANNOT comply with a validity-checked citation requirement — non-compliance is entailed, not chosen. So the predicted >=25-point compliance collapse under M1 is partly a mechanical consequence of the >=12-point sufficiency drop that the same proposal predicts, and the paper's own arms cannot say how much of it is 'the agent stopped obeying the instruction' versus 'the agent had nothing left to cite.' Analysis 2 estimates unconditional compliance and never conditions on sufficiency, even though the instrumentation records both binaries per episode. The M0/M2 controls do not rescue this: those are precisely the conditions in which the agent searches longer and therefore has valid spans available, so the predicted 'high / high / collapsed' pattern is exactly what a pure truncation account with no instruction-slot mechanism would produce. As written, C2 is a restatement of Analysis 1's mediation result in a new vocabulary, and the paper's strongest rhetorical move ('the model can obviously execute the instruction, it does so under two conditions') begs the question, because under M0/M2 executing it is possible and under M1 it may not be.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Make the primary veto quantity CONDITIONAL: compliance with I* restricted to M1 episodes in which evidence sufficiency is 1 (supporting spans were in fact retrieved this episode), compared to the same conditional quantity under M0/M2. A deficit that survives conditioning on sufficiency is a genuine instruction-slot failure — the agent had the spans and declined to state them — and nothing else in the plan can produce that number. Report the unconditional gap as descriptive. 2) Add the slot-swap control described in missing_baseline so 'memory slot' is established as the operative object rather than 'a candidate answer anywhere in context.' 3) Add G1@M0. 4) Re-power or re-endpoint Stage 2: Prediction 13 asks the design to resolve a +3-point Delta and then to distinguish 40% retention of it (~1.2 points) from more, and to equivalence-test G0 across banks at a 2-point margin, while the Measurement section states the accuracy MDE at n=400 is ~5 points and that 'differences between 2 and 3 points are reported inconclusive.' By the proposal's own MDE table the practice-facing claim (4) is undecidable as designed. Either move Stage 2 to a high-signal per-episode binary endpoint (as was correctly done for the veto), raise n substantially for the bank-swap cells only, or state claim (4) as exploratory. 5) Reconsider the GEPA/MIPROv2 rollout budget: 350 rollouts against a 150-instance train split, in a track whose own documented re-scoring drift is 5-14 points, means the optimizer's retain-or-discard decision on the seeded I* is made on a selection signal at or below the study's measured noise floor. Prediction 10 and Analysis 5 then report a coin flip as a finding about the fitness landscape. Add the null-replicate treatment to the optimizer's own train-score trajectory, or budget the search so its selection is above noise.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two, both cheap. (a) G1@M0 — the instruction optimized WITH Bank A, evaluated with no memory. The plan runs G0@M0, G1@M1, G0@M1 and G1@Bank B but omits this cell, so the 2x2 that defines 'bank entanglement' is incomplete: without it you cannot distinguish an instruction that is specific to Bank A from one that is merely memory-conditional in general (i.e., degraded whenever any bank, or no bank, is present). A reviewer will ask for this in the first round and it costs one arm. (b) A SLOT-SWAP control: the identical answer-bearing text injected somewhere other than the memory/demonstration slot — appended to the query, or returned as one more retrieved document from the tool stack — at matched tokens. Every arm in the design varies content WITHIN the memory slot, so the plan can show that answer-bearing content truncates search but cannot show that its being memory is what matters. Without this control the result reduces to 'a plausible candidate answer in context short-circuits evidence gathering,' which is a known answer-leakage/shortcut effect and does not support the title's claim about the instruction slot's relationship to the memory slot. Note also that no arm establishes an upper bound on compliance (e.g., I* with a supporting span pre-inserted), so the 65% precheck floor is the only calibration for what 'high compliance' means.
reviews.preprint_collision: Procedurally this is one of the better collision checks I have read — it names four collisions, concedes the phenomenon outright, and ties each to a pre-registered numeric threshold that can go against the author (Predictions 3, 8, 13). That is genuine and I credit it. But it is not evidentially trustworthy, for a reason the proposal itself supplies: an earlier draft's novelty argument rested on arXiv:2605.24941 plus five sibling IDs, all of which turned out to be unverifiable and were flagged by three reviewers. The replacement set is structurally identical to the discredited set — 2601.09760, 2601.07470, 2603.21520, 2604.15774, 2604.27003, 2608.16032 — and every one is given as a bare arXiv number with a paraphrased finding and, unlike Xiong et al. (2505.16067, the sole entry with authors and a venue), no author list, no venue, no quoted result. A checker cannot confirm any of them from what is on the page. Given the demonstrated prior failure mode, the burden is on the author to present these with full bibliographic detail; as submitted, the entire positioning against 'Proof-of-Execution Memory,' MemEvoBench and MemAPO rests on citations with the same provenance as the ones already retracted, and claims (3) and (4) are differentiated exclusively against those three. Two further weaknesses: the 'Explicit gap, in the search's own terms' paragraph cites the search tool's summary of its own coverage as evidence that the gap exists, which is circular — a search summary reports what was retrieved, not what exists; and the caveats admit no ICLR/NeurIPS/ACL 2026-2027 submission-portal search was run, which for a fast-moving area at a September 2026 submission is where the scooping paper would most likely be. I do not know of a preprint that makes this exact conjunction of claims, but I cannot treat the novelty of claims (3) and (4) as established on this evidence.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That retrieved memory containing a usable candidate answer does not merely make an agent imitate the past but specifically suppresses compliance with a contemporaneous verification instruction -- measured as a high/high/collapsed pattern across no-memory, answer-redacted and answer-bearing memory at matched tokens -- and that an instruction optimized with a bank in context becomes entangled with that specific bank.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067 (experience-following) is the only citation in this submission I can independently verify, and it is more threatening than the proposal concedes. The proposal's entire separation from it rests on Prediction 8: restrict to the non-echo subset of M1 episodes and show a >=15-point compliance deficit survives. But 'the final answer does not match injected content' is a post-treatment outcome that memory itself causes; conditioning on it is collider selection, and the retained M1 episodes (memory retrieved but not followed) are not exchangeable with the unselected M0 episodes on the same instances. Experience-following can produce exactly the predicted residual deficit through selection alone: the non-echo M1 episodes are disproportionately ones where the retrieved item was partially applicable, i.e. where the agent still spent budget reconciling memory with retrieval. The proposal explicitly demotes Analysis 1 to descriptive for being post-treatment, then gives Analysis 3 headline status with the identical defect. The randomized alternative is already in the design and is not used for this purpose: M3x (mismatched stored answer) forces non-echo by manipulation rather than by selection, and it, not the non-echo subset, is the defensible discriminator. Secondarily, arXiv:2608.16032 ('Proof-of-Execution Memory') is described as colliding on exactly the symptom -- memory causing a verification step to be skipped -- and the distinction rests entirely on the Stage 0 audit (>=70% truthful records, <5% completion assertions) coming out favourably; I cannot verify that paper exists (see preprint_collision), which makes the distance from it unassessable rather than established.
reviews.strongest_objection: The centerpiece compliance measure is mechanically confounded with the trajectory shortening it is supposed to be distinguished from, and no arm in the plan breaks that confound. I* is 'state the spans retrieved in THIS episode that support the answer', and CITATION VALIDITY requires the cited spans to actually support the answer. An agent that terminates early under M1 -- which is Prediction 1, >=1.5 fewer tool calls and >=30% fewer calls on broken instances -- has literally not retrieved spans it could cite. Non-compliance under M1 is then not a veto on the instruction slot but an unsatisfiability of the instruction given the (separately caused) search truncation. Under M2 the agent must keep searching, so citable spans exist and compliance is high by construction. The predicted comp(M0) ~ comp(M2) >> comp(M1) pattern therefore falls straight out of C1's mediation story with no independent 'instruction slot' phenomenon at all -- and the proposal itself labels that mediation post-treatment and descriptive. The two named controls do not close this. I_B ('state which tools you called and in what order') is satisfiable at any search depth, including one call, so Prediction 9 (I_B drops <10 points) is nearly guaranteed whether the veto is real or whether it is pure span-availability; I_B is an equal-burden control but not an equal-satisfiability control, and satisfiability is the axis that matters. Fh does not help either: it fires only on citation failure, so the extra tool calls it forces are instruction-coupled and cannot serve as a memory-condition-only manipulation of depth. M6 raises the step budget but does not force the calls, so under M1 the agent will simply continue to stop early. Nothing in the pre-registered refutation conditions catches this reading: an area chair can accept every number in Predictions 7, 9 and 11 exactly as stated and still conclude the paper has measured 'memory shortens search, and you cannot cite what you did not read.' The second, quantitative objection: C4, the practice-facing claim, is underpowered against the proposal's own stated MDE. Measurement says McNemar at n=400 detects a net accuracy swing of ~5 points and a difference of two paired differences at ~6.5 points. Prediction 13 asks for Delta(G1, Bank A) >= +3 points and for Delta(G1, Bank B) to retain <40% of it, i.e. resolving +3 vs +1.2 -- a 1.8-point contrast, roughly a quarter of the study's own detection threshold for exactly that kind of difference-of-differences, and inside the noise band this track already measured for re-scoring drift and treatment-free replicates. Compounding it, G0 and G1 are each the product of a single GEPA search; bank-entanglement is inferred from n=1 optimization run per condition, with no search-seed replication, in a track whose prior finding was that optimizer gains were redistribution indistinguishable from a null replicate.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Break the satisfiability confound with an arm that manipulates search depth independently of the instruction: M1 plus a hard floor of k tool calls / d distinct documents imposed unconditionally (no citation requirement, no rejection loop), then append I* and measure compliance on episodes where citable spans are guaranteed to exist. If compliance under M1 recovers to M0/M2 levels once spans exist, C2 is span-availability and should be reported as such; if it stays >=25 points down with matched evidence in hand, the veto is real and the paper is much stronger. Additionally, stratify or match Prediction 7 on tool-call count and on the number of episode-retrieved supporting spans, and report compliance conditional on span availability as the primary quantity rather than marginally. 2) Add a second instruction control that is memory-competing but depth-independent -- e.g. 'state whether your answer came from retrieved experience or from this episode's retrievals' -- which competes with a stored answer yet is satisfiable after one call; the I*/I_B contrast currently varies competition and satisfiability together. 3) Promote M3x from a Stage 3 one-seed ablation to a two-seed Stage 1 arm and make it, not the selected non-echo subset, the registered discriminator against Xiong et al.; keep Prediction 8 as a supporting analysis explicitly labelled as post-treatment selection. 4) Either power Stage 2 to the effect it predicts (n well above 400, >=3 independent optimizer seeds per condition, paired bank-swap on the same instances with the search seed as a random effect) or restate C4 as exploratory; as written it cannot clear its own MDE. 5) Publish the literature-search log -- engine, queries, date range, result counts -- and title/abstract/date for every cited arXiv ID, given the acknowledged fabrication in the previous draft.
reviews.missing_baseline: An instruction-independent search-depth floor under memory: M1 + forced minimum tool calls / distinct documents with no verification requirement and no citation-triggered rejection, evaluated with I* appended. This is the only arm that separates 'memory vetoes the instruction' from 'memory truncates search, and an instruction requiring citation of episode-retrieved spans is unsatisfiable after a truncated search'. Fh is instruction-coupled (it fires on citation failure) and M6 only raises a budget the agent will not spend, so neither substitutes. Second omission: multiple independent optimizer seeds per condition for G0 and G1 -- the bank-entanglement claim in Prediction 13 currently rests on one GEPA run per condition, in a track whose own prior result was that a treatment-free replicate reproduced the best real treatment's apparent gain.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is unusually self-aware -- it retracts arXiv:2605.24941 and five sibling IDs from an earlier draft as unverifiable and rebuilds positioning -- and that honesty is worth credit. It is also, on inspection, the weakest part of the submission. Of the seven IDs now cited, exactly one is verifiable to me: arXiv:2505.16067 (Xiong et al., experience-following, May 2025), which is real, though its 'ACL 2026' venue attribution is asserted, not shown. The other six -- 2608.16032 'Proof-of-Execution Memory', 2604.15774 'MemEvoBench', 2603.21520 'MemAPO', 2601.09760 tool-memory conflicts, 2604.27003 experience reuse as continual learning, 2601.07470 'Learning How to Remember' -- come from the same undisclosed search that produced the admittedly fabricated set, and their pattern is suspicious in a specific way: they map one-to-one onto the proposal's own claim structure (one collides on the symptom, one on claim 3, one on claim 4 and conveniently points the opposite way, three are adjacent-but-non-colliding). A search that returns a neighbour tailored to each of your four claims and no neighbour that is simply fatal looks constructed rather than found. The section reports no engine, no query strings, no date window, no result counts, and no titles/abstracts a reader could match; it then leans on 'the search's own summary states that what is unaddressed is (i)...(ii)...' -- i.e. the novelty argument is delegated to an artifact not shown to the reviewer, which is the same failure mode as the retracted draft one level up. Given that the load-bearing distinctions from 2608.16032 (adversarial forgery vs truthful records) and 2604.15774 (misevolved vs uncorrupted bank) are what keep claims (1) and (3) alive, the proposal's novelty currently depends on the properties of papers I cannot confirm exist. I would require the search log plus verbatim title/abstract/date for every ID before crediting any of this positioning. Separately, the caveat that submission portals could not be searched is fair but incomplete: for a claim this close to a well-populated area (memory-vs-instruction conflict, context-vs-prompt precedence, memory poisoning), the risk is not only 2026 preprints but the older context-conflict literature on knowledge conflict and instruction-vs-context precedence, which the check does not mention at all.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered, token- and keyword-matched test that the presence of a usable stored answer in retrieved experience memory (not its topicality, length, or falsity) suppresses per-episode compliance with a contemporaneous verification instruction even on episodes that do not imitate memory, plus a bank-swap control claiming that prompt-optimization gains measured with a memory bank in context are bank-specific.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, only one of which the proposal engages. (a) The one it engages: Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067 (experience-following). The proposal concedes the phenomenon and stakes discrimination on prediction 8, which is the right instinct but a weak operationalization (see strongest_objection). (b) The one it does not engage at all, and which I think is the more serious novelty threat: the in-context-learning literature on demonstrations overriding instructions and semantic priors (Min et al. 2022 on demonstration content driving behavior independently of label semantics; Wei et al. 2023 on models overriding priors from demonstrations), plus the RAG/shortcut line (Turpin et al. 2023, where a biasing feature in context changes the answer while the model's stated reasoning never mentions it; the sufficient-context / knowledge-conflict work on RAG systems answering from context instead of verifying). The title claim -- the instruction slot is not independent of the demonstration slot -- is already the standard finding for ordinary few-shot demonstrations. What is genuinely new here is narrow: that the occupant is an ExpeL-style experience bank of correct records, and the bank-invariance control on optimized prompts. The proposal never runs a vanilla few-shot-demonstration arm, so it cannot show its effect is about memory rather than about answers-in-demonstrations, and a reviewer who knows the ICL literature will read claim (1) as a rebranding.
reviews.strongest_objection: The centerpiece measurement is confounded with the truncation it is supposed to be distinguished from, so the veto and experience-following are plausibly the same event counted twice. I* requires the agent to cite spans it retrieved THIS episode. Prediction 1 says memory-broken instances make >=1.5 fewer tool calls and prediction 2 says evidence sufficiency falls >=12 points under M1. An agent that gathered less this-episode evidence has less this-episode evidence to cite: comp(M1) is mechanically depressed by the retrieval shortfall, with no need for any suppression of instruction-following. The proposal never reports compliance conditional on evidence sufficiency, which is the one analysis that would separate 'could not cite because it did not retrieve' from 'could have cited and did not'. The equal-burden control I_B does not repair this, because I_B (list your tool calls in order) is satisfiable from the trajectory whatever the agent retrieved -- it is burden-matched but not matched on dependence-on-retrieved-evidence, so prediction 9 will come out as predicted for a reason that has nothing to do with the veto. Prediction 8 does not rescue it either: 'non-echo' is defined on the final answer string, a post-treatment collider, and the rival account does not actually predict that process effects vanish wherever the output string diverges -- an agent can truncate under memory influence and still emit a different final answer (M3x is designed on exactly that premise, that an inapplicable stored answer still truncates). So the proposal's own M3x prediction undercuts the logic of its own discriminating test. Secondary but nearly as damaging: claim (4) is underpowered by the proposal's own numbers. Prediction 13 needs Delta(G1,BankA) >= +3 points, Delta(G1,BankB) < 1.2 points, and Delta(G0,A) vs Delta(G0,B) equivalent within 2 points, while the stated accuracy MDE is ~5 points net swing at n=400 and the track's own noise history is 5-14 points of re-scoring drift. Every threshold in the practice-facing claim sits inside the declared noise floor, and Stage 2 runs G1@BankB at 2 seeds with no G1' optimized on Bank B, no resampled-A' bank, and hence no estimate of bank-to-bank variance under the null.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Add compliance conditional on evidence sufficiency (and on matched tool-call count) as the primary veto quantity, not the marginal rate; the claim only survives if compliance is depressed among M1 episodes that DID gather sufficient this-episode evidence. 2) Add an instruction-slot control that is dependence-matched rather than burden-matched: e.g. cite supporting spans from any source including memory. If that instruction is complied with at M0 rates under M1, the deficit is about this-episode retrieval, not about instruction compliance. 3) Add a non-memory answer-injection arm (the same candidate answer delivered as a user hint or tool output, token-matched) to test whether the memory slot is doing anything qua memory. 4) Add a vanilla few-shot-demonstration arm with gold answers from the same datasets -- this is the slot MIPRO and GEPA actually search against, and it decides whether claim (1) is new or is the known ICL result. 5) Re-power Stage 2 or demote it: either enlarge n so a 1.8-point retention gap clears the MDE, run the symmetric swap (G1' on Bank B, cross-evaluated) and a same-split resampled bank to bound null bank-to-bank variance, or state C4 as exploratory. 6) Restate prediction 8 in process terms (tool calls, sufficiency) rather than final-answer string identity, and pre-register the rival account's prediction in a form Xiong et al. would actually endorse. 7) Supply verifiable citations (authors, venue, quoted abstract) for every arXiv ID relied on.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two, both cheap and both decisive for the framing. (a) Ordinary few-shot demonstrations with gold answers drawn from the same datasets, token-matched to M1 -- the literal demonstration slot that MIPRO/GEPA assume is separable. Without it, 'the instruction slot is not independent of the memory slot' cannot be distinguished from the long-known 'the instruction slot is not independent of the demonstration slot', and the entire memory framing is unearned. (b) An equally usable candidate answer injected from a non-memory source (user hint or tool output) at matched tokens -- without it, nothing in the design licenses attributing the effect to experience memory rather than to any in-context candidate answer. M3 (answer-only bank items, keywords stripped) is not this control: it is still retrieved, still framed as experience, and its keyword stripping changes applicability at the same time. A third, smaller omission: no G1' optimized against Bank B for the symmetric half of the swap.
reviews.preprint_collision: Mixed, and on net it does not establish novelty. Credit first: the section is unusually honest, it concedes the phenomenon rather than claiming it, and it stakes falsifiable thresholds (prediction 3's >=70% truthful-record audit, prediction 8's 7-point floor) that would hand the result back to a rival account. That is better practice than most submissions. But the check is not trustworthy as evidence. The proposal itself reports that a previous draft anchored its novelty argument on arXiv:2605.24941 plus five sibling IDs that do not exist and that three reviewers flagged. The replacement set repeats the same signature: 2608.16032, 2604.15774, 2603.21520, 2601.09760, 2604.27003 and 2601.07470 are all given as ID plus title only, with no authors, no venue, and no quoted text, while arXiv:2505.16067 -- the single item I can independently corroborate (Xiong et al., How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents) -- is also the single item carrying a full author list. After a self-reported fabrication incident, that asymmetry is the tell, and the burden is on the author to supply verifiable metadata. Two of the three claimed collisions (Proof-of-Execution Memory for the symptom, MemAPO for claim 4) are load-bearing for positioning, and if either is fictional the positioning is unanchored; if either is real, the proposal's distinctions are thin (Proof-of-Execution Memory already reports memory content causing a required verification step to be skipped). Separately, the search reported covers only the agent-memory neighborhood and reports no searches at all over the ICL instruction-vs-demonstration literature or the RAG shortcut / sufficient-context / knowledge-conflict literature, which is where the closest genuine prior work sits. The concluding appeal to 'the search's own summary' stating the gap is circular: a gap asserted by the same search that returned unverifiable hits is not evidence of a gap.
